summary: Savannah Airstrip (KHX) is a small bush airstrip serving Kihihi in southwestern Uganda, acting as a key gateway to Bwindi Impenetrable National Park, one of the world's premier mountain gorilla trekking destinations. Its remote location near the Bwindi forest makes it a vital access point for safari operators and conservation travelers flying in from Entebbe. The unpaved runway supports light charter aircraft operated primarily by domestic carriers serving the tourism circuit.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines fly into Savannah Airstrip?
A: Domestic charter operators such as Aerolink Uganda typically serve KHX with light aircraft from Entebbe International Airport. Flights are usually part of pre-booked safari packages.

Q: How long is the flight from Entebbe to KHX?
A: The flight takes roughly 1 hour and 15 minutes by charter aircraft, offering spectacular aerial views of the Ugandan countryside and Lake Victoria basin.

Q: What is the runway surface like at KHX?
A: Savannah Airstrip has a grass/marston mat surface suitable for small propeller aircraft. Schedules can be affected by heavy rain, particularly during the two wet seasons.

Q: Can I get gorilla trekking permits at Kihihi?
A: Permits cannot be purchased at the airstrip itself; they must be reserved in advance through the Uganda Wildlife Authority or a registered tour operator, ideally months ahead for peak season.
transport_tips: Most lodges near Bwindi Impenetrable National Park arrange 4x4 transfers from the airstrip, typically taking 45-90 minutes depending on the camp's location within the park sector. Shared shuttle services are rarely available, so pre-booking a vehicle with your lodge is highly recommended. Road conditions can be rough and muddy, particularly after rainfall, so plan extra travel time.
local_tip: Pack a light rain jacket in your day bag for the open-air transfer from the airstrip to your lodge—the Bwindi microclimate is notoriously wet, and the short drive crosses misty forested ridges where sudden showers are common even in the dry season.
